title: Biggest Number Swapping Same-Parity Digits
statement:
You get a positive integer num. You may swap any two of its digits as many times as you like, but only when both digits are odd or both are even.

Return the largest number you can reach.

examples.why: The 8 cannot jump to the front: the front digit 3 is odd and 8 is even. The best you can do is swap 6 and 8.
The odd slots (5, 7, 1) take 7, 5, 1 in that order; the even slots (2, 4) take 4, 2.
Sorting all digits would give 4433, but no odd digit may trade places with an even one.

hints: Split the digits into two teams: odd digits and even digits. Can a digit ever leave the set of positions its team occupies?
Within one team, any rearrangement is reachable with swaps. The positions held by each team never change.
Sort each team from largest to smallest, then walk the original positions and fill each one with the next digit from its team.

explain.intuition:
Swaps never mix the teams, so the set of positions holding odd digits is fixed, and so is the set holding even digits. Inside one team, though, swaps let you reach any order at all.

To make the number as large as possible, the earliest position should get the biggest digit it is allowed to have. That means: in the odd positions, place the odd digits in descending order; in the even positions, the even digits in descending order. It is the same as sorting two separate lists and zipping them back by position.
steps: Turn num into a list of digits.
Collect the odd digits and the even digits into two lists, each sorted in descending order.
Walk the original digits left to right. If the digit there is odd, take the next odd digit from its list, otherwise the next even one.
Join the digits back into a number.
pitfalls: Sorting all digits together: 3344 would become 4433, which mixes parities.
Assigning the sorted odd digits to the first few positions instead of to the positions that were odd originally.
Thinking only adjacent swaps are allowed. Any two same-parity digits can swap, wherever they are.

complexity.time: O(d log d), d = number of digits (at most 10)

solutions.title: Swap whenever it helps
solutions.idea: For each position, look right for a larger digit of the same parity and swap the largest one in. This is a selection sort run inside each parity team.

solutions.title: Sort each parity team separately
solutions.idea: Odd and even positions stay fixed. Sort each team in descending order and deal them back into their own positions.

followups: Digits may only swap when they are adjacent and have the same parity. Does the answer change?
Instead of parity, swaps are allowed between digits joined by a given list of pairs of positions. What structure finds the groups that can be sorted freely?
lcTitle: Largest Number After Digit Swaps by Parity
